title: US Hands Over 10 Individuals Sought by Mexico for Various Serious Crimes and Organized Crime
author: Arturo Sánchez Jiménez
content:
_This article by[Arturo Sánchez
Jiménez](https://www.jornada.com.mx/autores/Arturo%20S%C3%A1nchez%20Jim%C3%A9nez)
originally appeared in the [August 25, 2026 edition of La
Jornada](https://www.jornada.com.mx/noticia/2026/08/25/politica/eu-entrega-a-
mexico-a-10-individuos-buscados-por-varios-delitos-graves-y-delincuencia-
organizada), Mexico’s premier left-wing daily newspaper._

Ten Mexican fugitives wanted for serious crimes—including kidnapping, drug
trafficking, and weapons possession—were handed over to Mexico by U.S.
authorities in recent days, the United States ambassador, retired colonel
Ronald Johnson, said Tuesday.

The Washington envoy explained on social media that the 10 individuals were
wanted by the justice system in several states of the country for serious
crimes, among them kidnapping, drug- and weapons-related offenses, as well as
activities linked to organized crime organizations.

**“Our cooperation is delivering results: fewer criminals on our streets,
greater accountability, and safer communities,”** wrote Johnson, who
accompanied the message with photographs of the detainees, most of them
handcuffed and guarded by police and military personnel at border points.

The ambassador stressed that bilateral coordination between the two countries
has made it possible to reduce the spaces of impunity for those facing
criminal charges. **“When the United States and Mexico work together,
criminals have nowhere to hide,”** he maintained.
